ip_top_stories.title: Over 100 Authors Sue Anthropic, Claim AI Firm Used Pirated Books
ip_top_stories.summary: More than 100 authors have filed suit against Anthropic, alleging the AI company used pirated books to train its models. The case adds to a growing wave of copyright litigation targeting major AI developers over their use of unlicensed creative works.

ip_top_stories.title: Eleonora Rosati, lawyer: 'Artists are already thinking about how to protect themselves from AI; Taylor Swift has registered her voice'
ip_top_stories.summary: IP lawyer Eleonora Rosati discusses how artists are proactively seeking legal protection against AI, noting that Taylor Swift has taken the step of registering her voice. The interview covers emerging strategies creators are using to safeguard their identities and outputs in the face of generative AI.

ip_top_stories.title: Investors sue Adobe execs over AI copyright statements
ip_top_stories.summary: Investors have filed a lawsuit against Adobe executives, alleging they made misleading statements about the company's exposure to AI copyright infringement claims. The case focuses on whether Adobe adequately disclosed legal risks associated with its AI-generated content tools.

ip_top_stories.title: APRA AMCOS Reveals Australian And New Zealand Songs Found In AI Training Datasets
ip_top_stories.summary: Australian and New Zealand music rights organisation APRA AMCOS has disclosed that songs by local artists have been identified in AI training datasets without authorisation. The findings intensify calls for licensing frameworks and stronger protections for music creators in the region.

ip_top_stories.title: Charity Advising Canberra on AI Copyright Laws Funded by Anthropic-Linked Donors
ip_top_stories.summary: A charity providing advice to the Australian government on AI copyright policy has been found to receive funding from donors linked to Anthropic, raising concerns about conflicts of interest in the legislative process. The revelation comes as Australia considers significant changes to its copyright framework to accommodate AI.

ip_further_links.title: German court holds Google liable for AI hallucination: Read the full decision here
ip_further_links.summary: A German court has found Google liable for an AI-generated hallucination, with the full decision now available, marking a significant ruling on AI accountability and potential defamation implications.

ip_further_links.title: Bombay High Court allows Preity Zinta to sue online platforms for infringement of content produced with AI
ip_further_links.summary: The Bombay High Court has permitted actor Preity Zinta to proceed with a lawsuit against online platforms for infringing AI-produced content, in a notable ruling on the protectability of AI-assisted creative works.

ip_further_links.title: Calif. Senate Votes to Advance AI Copyright Bill Backed by Voice Actors
ip_further_links.summary: The California Senate has voted to advance an AI copyright bill supported by voice actors, which would provide protections against unauthorised use of performers' voices in AI-generated content.

ip_further_links.title: AI Deepfake Law NO FAKES Act Advances in Congress With Key Senate Committee Vote
ip_further_links.summary: The NO FAKES Act, which targets AI-generated deepfakes of individuals, has cleared a key Senate committee vote, moving the legislation closer to becoming federal law in the United States.

ip_further_links.title: The novel legal strategy that Taylor Swift, Matthew McConaughey are using to fight AI
ip_further_links.summary: Taylor Swift and Matthew McConaughey are among celebrities employing a novel legal strategy — including voice and likeness registration — to protect themselves against unauthorised AI use of their identities.

ip_further_links.title: Rights holders and generative AI companies: infringement risks meet competition pressure
ip_further_links.summary: An analysis examines the mounting tension between rights holders and generative AI firms, exploring how infringement risks intersect with commercial competition pressures on both sides of the debate.

ip_further_links.title: How US courts are addressing fair use questions in AI training and copyright disputes
ip_further_links.summary: A review of how US courts are approaching fair use defences raised by AI companies in copyright disputes over training data, highlighting emerging judicial trends.

ip_further_links.title: News Orgs Must Give Cohere AI Use Policies
ip_further_links.summary: News organisations have been told they must provide Cohere with their AI use policies, raising questions about how publishers' content is being used for AI training and what transparency obligations exist.

ip_further_links.title: Big Tech Is a Thief and Liar, Says NYT Publisher
ip_further_links.summary: The publisher of The New York Times has publicly accused Big Tech companies of stealing content and being dishonest about their use of publisher material for AI training.

ip_further_links.title: Adobe Faces Derivative Claims For AI Copyright Infringement
ip_further_links.summary: Adobe is facing derivative claims for AI copyright infringement, with shareholders alleging the company failed to adequately address or disclose its exposure to intellectual property liability from AI tools.
